title: Resident BRAINK root identity is independent of HTTP/TCP carrier endpoint
statement: For a fixed resident root graph and fixed machine projection, changing the HTTP/TCP listener endpoint or process instance does not redefine the resident BRAINK root graph identity; the carrier is projection-only.
invariants: resident graph digest is derived from resident root state, not HTTP host/port
BRAINK_ROOT/SERVER_ROOT/CLOUD_ROOT state digests remain authoritative over carrier observations
fabric join rejects a mismatched resident graph digest

falsification.experiment: Instantiate the same resident graph through two different process instances and carrier endpoints on the same machine projection, then compare resident graph digest/root digests and complete a signed join against each endpoint.
falsification.pass_condition: Both carrier instances expose identical resident graph/root digests and accept the same expected resident graph digest while their carrier endpoint/process identity differs.
falsification.fail_condition: Changing process or HTTP/TCP endpoint changes resident graph/root identity or allows a mismatched graph to be accepted.

proof_requirements.description: Resident graph/root digests remain identical across carrier endpoint/process replacement.
Join rejects a deliberately wrong resident graph digest.
Carrier replacement proof repeats without identity drift.

invalid_overclaims: This does not prove host-independent remote-node identity because current remote node_id includes machine_material().
This does not prove cross-machine migration.
This does not prove public Internet reachability.
A workflow trigger or queued runner is not execution evidence.
next_experiments: Introduce a logical-computer identity above machine projection and test preservation across two independent hosts.
Compare carrier replacement latency and state continuity with a conventional endpoint-bound service identity baseline.
